methods.label: Simplify while retaining the excluded input
methods.explanation:
At an intersection, both formulas must be defined and give the same \(y\)-value. The denominator of the first formula requires \(x\ne2\). For these allowed inputs,
\[
\frac{x^2-4}{x-2}
=\frac{(x-2)(x+2)}{x-2}
=x+2.
\]
Thus an intersection would require \(x+2=2x\), giving \(x=2\). But that input makes the original denominator zero, so it cannot give an intersection. The graphs have \(\boxed{\text{no points in common, choice C}}\).
